adult.int:age*hours: the hours effect is weaker for older people
adult.int:age*married: the age effect is weaker inside marriage
adult.int:capgain*married: the capital-gain threshold acts more strongly for the married
adult.int:sex*married: the gap between women and men is larger outside marriage
adult.lin:age: older people are less likely to have a low income
adult.lin:capgain: capital gains lower the chance of a low income
adult.lin:caploss: recorded capital losses lower the chance of a low income
adult.lin:country: offsets for single countries of birth, mostly small groups
adult.lin:edu: each extra year of schooling lowers the chance of a low income
adult.lin:edulevel: offsets for single education levels beyond the years-of-schooling line
adult.lin:fnlwgt: the survey sampling weight, not a personal attribute
adult.lin:hours: longer working weeks lower the chance of a low income
adult.lin:household: low income likelier outside marriage: husbands and wives sit well below the unmarried
adult.lin:sex: women are more likely to have a low income than otherwise similar men
adult.lin:work: executive, managerial and professional work sit below; service and handling work and missing job records above
adult.shape:age: the fall with age is steep for the young and turns back later in life
adult.shape:capgain: past about $6,000 of capital gain the chance of a low income drops steeply
adult.shape:caploss: bends in the capital-loss effect across loss amounts
adult.shape:fnlwgt: bends in the survey sampling weight
adult.shape:hours: short weeks raise the chance of a low income more than long weeks lower it

churn.int:csc*day: the service-call rise is strongest for light daytime users
churn.int:csc*intlplan: service calls with the international plan
churn.int:csc*vmail: service calls read with the voice-mail plan
churn.int:day*eve: the combined bill: evening minutes raise churn more for heavy day users
churn.int:day*night: day and night use read together
churn.int:day*vmail: heavy daytime use matters mostly without a voice-mail plan
churn.int:eve*csc: evening use read with service calls
churn.int:intlplan*intl: plan holders churn when they use the plan heavily (many minutes) or rarely (few calls)
churn.lin:acct: churn rises slightly with account length
churn.lin:csc: churn rises with each call to customer service
churn.lin:day: churn rises with daytime minutes (a charge is a fixed multiple of its minutes)
churn.lin:daycalls: churn rises slightly with the number of day calls
churn.lin:intlcalls: churn falls slightly with the number of international calls
churn.lin:night: churn rises slightly with night minutes
churn.lin:state: a separate offset for some states
churn.lin:vmail: a voice-mail plan (and its messages) lowers churn
churn.shape:csc: churn flat over the first calls, steep from 4 calls
churn.shape:day: heavy daytime use: churn climbs steeply above about 300 minutes

heart100.BP: a threshold, alone (3 of 10 units) or with exercise angina, ST slope, thallium scan or heart rate (others in single units)
heart100.ST depression: counted only past a threshold in 2 of 3 units
heart100.ST slope: a step, read with cholesterol, chest pain, exercise angina or sex
heart100.age: the rise of risk with age slows past an age (5 of 6 units)
heart100.exang: a gate, read with sex in 3 of 4 seeds (on mostly for women in 2)
heart100.max HR: a bend or gate in peak heart rate
heart100.resting ECG: the resting ECG through a switching unit
heart100.thal: the thallium scan read through a gate, with ST depression in 9 of 11 units
heart100.thal × age: the thallium scan read with age
